page: OVHcloud c2-7 is a compute-optimized instance hosted on a KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, offering 2 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory capacity is fixed at 7.0 GB of RAM (3.5 GB per core), and local storage includes a 50 GB SSD. Baseline network bandwidth is listed at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPUs are bundled.

Hardware capabilities feature instruction extensions such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while lacking newer vector and matrix sets such as AVX-512 and AMX. The CPU cache configuration provides 32 KB of L1d, 4 MB of L2, and 16 MB of L3 cache. In compute benchmarks, the legacy architecture shows subdued throughput, with stress-ng recording 864.27 on single-core and 1718.26 on multi-core tests, placing it in the bottom 10%. Geekbench yields 1076.0 in single-core and 1876.0 in multi-core performance, reflecting the older generation instruction execution efficiency.

Memory throughput registers at 20.03 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 16.03 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific benchmarks indicate modest capabilities, such as Redis SET operations at 2.71 million ops/sec and static web serving throughput of 2.42 GB/sec. On lightweight natural language models, text generation for a 135M parameter LLM achieves an average 74.86 tokens/sec, though prompt processing reaches only 212.61 tokens/sec.

Given its older CPU architecture, lack of bundled public IPv4, and low benchmark percentiles across both compute and memory tests, the c2-7 presents clear performance tradeoffs. It is best positioned for low-intensity, non-latency-critical general tasks, internal staging environments, small batch scripts, or lightweight utility services that require dedicated cores but do not demand modern processing performance.
